> 我有三寶，持而保之：一曰慈，二曰儉，三曰不敢為天下先.

Chapter 66 gave a position. Chapter 67 gives what you hold to stand there: three treasures.

They are usually taught as three virtues — compassion, frugality, humility. And the third one hides a mistranslation that has stood for a thousand years.

## 長 is duration, not rank

> 不敢為天下先，故能成器長.

Almost every modern reading renders 長 as "chief" — so the line becomes "therefore he can become the head of everything."

But 說文 gives 長 as: 長，久遠也. Long, far in time.

So the sentence is: not taking the front, and therefore able to complete things — and to make them last.

長 measures time, not position.

## Once that is right, the three treasures change category

They stop being three virtues and become three constraints on how to last:

- 慈 — not "kindness." Warmth toward what is alive: a heart with something growing in it, protective of life.
- 儉 — not "cheapness." The strands gathered into one binding: everything scattered in, drawn to a single cord.
- 不敢為天下先 — not "yielding." Not taking the front position, and thereby lasting.

None of the three is moral. All three are ways of continuing to exist.

## And the returns

慈，故能勇 — because he protects life, he can be brave. Bravery in defense is different from bravery in display: it has an object.

儉，故能廣 — because nothing is scattered, there is room to be broad. Breadth bought by spending is not breadth.

不敢為天下先，故能成器長 — not taking the front, so the thing gets finished and stays finished.

## 肖: unlike the father

> 天下皆謂我道大，似不肖. 夫唯大，故似不肖.

肖: 骨肉相似也 — bone and flesh resembling another. And 說文 adds: 不似其先，故曰不肖也 — not resembling his forebear, therefore 不肖.

不肖 is the commonest insult in pre-Qin speech: the son who does not look like his father, the disappointment.

So "everyone says my way is great but it doesn't look like anything" is not praise. It is a complaint. It means: we cannot place it.

Laozi accepts it: exactly — because it is great, it does not resemble anything. If it resembled something, it would long ago have become small.

## 今舍慈且勇，舍儉且廣，舍後且先，死矣

Drop the protection and keep the bravery; drop the gathering and keep the breadth; drop the rear and take the front — that is death.

And 死矣 is not a threat. Each of the three is a state that cannot be sustained without its base.

## 夫慈，以戰則勝，以守則固

With 慈: attack and it prevails; defend and it holds.

The chapter is not claiming compassion wins battles by morale. It is claiming that the one fighting to protect something specific has a criterion that the one fighting for position does not.

天將救之，以慈衛之 — when heaven is going to save someone, 慈 is what guards him.

## The internal order

Note that the three treasures are in ascending order of difficulty, and descending order of visibility.

慈 is felt. 儉 is seen in what you don't have. 不敢為天下先 has no visible sign at all — it is only noticeable as an absence of something that did not happen.

## A test

Take the last thing you finished that lasted. Ask which of the three was doing the work. Almost always the third, and almost always uncredited.
